import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Prepare the dataset
csv_data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set a professional and clean style for the visualization
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="talk")

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create a multi-dimensional scatter plot (bubble chart)
# x-axis: megapixels
# y-axis: price
# color: brand
# size: max_iso (a key performance indicator)
# style: body_type
scatter_plot = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='brand',
    size='max_iso',
    style='body_type',
    sizes=(200, 2000),  # Control the range of bubble sizes
    palette='viridis',
    alpha=0.8,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=1,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Enhancements for Clarity and Insight ---

# Add annotations to each point for immediate identification
for i in range(df.shape[0]):
    ax.text(
        x=df.megapixels[i] + 0.7,
        y=df.price_usd[i],
        s=f"{df.brand[i]} ({df.model_year[i]})",
        fontdict=dict(color='black', size=11, style='italic')
    )

# Set a clear, descriptive title and labels
ax.set_title('Camera Market Analysis: Price, Megapixels, and ISO Performance', fontsize=20, pad=20, weight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Megapixels (MP)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Format the y-axis to display as currency
formatter = mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: f'${x:,.0f}')
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FormatStrFormatter('%.0f MP'))


# Improve the legend
# Move the legend outside the plot area to prevent it from covering data points
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax.legend(handles, labels, bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0., title='Features')


# Adjust layout to ensure all elements (like the legend) fit neatly
fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1])

# Save the final visualization to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
